newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's real drops 0.48 pct on dollar outflows.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's real drops 0.48 pct on dollar outflows.

text.p: Brazil's real dropped 0.48 percent to close at 1.0285 per dollar in the commercial foreign exchange market, mostly due to dollar outflows, dealers said.

Preliminary figures for commercial and financial foreign exchange contracts showed a Thursday deficit of around $60 million, but dealers estimated the deficit will be bigger when the banks finish the registration of all operations for the day.
In late afternoon, the Central Bank sold dollars at 1.0285 per dollar to supply the market, they added.

The Columbus Day holiday on Monday in the United States was one factor causing dollar outflows. Due to the holiday, operations made today will be settled Tuesday instead of Monday. Also, exporters preferred to delay their transactions for at least one more day, reducing dollar inflows, dealers said.
In the floating exchange rate market, the real ended flat at 1.0293 per dollar.
In the illegal parallel market, the real fell 0.48 percent to close at 1.045 per greenback, mostly due to an increase in the dollar demand, traders said.
